final.summary: Recommended: optimizer:throughput. Peak 90th pct core temp 37.99 °C (limit 38.0), tightest margin 0.00 °C, 86% of priority-weighted work done.
reasons: **Heat is right at the limit.** This plan gets about 86% of the important work done, but on the hottest stretch, crew body temperatures are expected to reach the safety limit with no room to spare. One more hot task or a slower break could push someone over, so watch for heat signs closely, enforce water and shade breaks, and don't add work.

**Storm stop and new-hire limits are built in.** Everyone comes inside from 1:30 to 3:00 because of lightning and severe thunderstorms. Kofi is new and not used to the heat yet, so he won't be given the hardest physical jobs during the hot part of the day.

**Two safer options are available.** (1) Give some of the load to Jada, who is currently free, and lighten Kofi's work. This runs slightly cooler but gets a bit less done (about 83%). (2) Move the trenching to the cool morning and save indoor jobs for later. This gets the same 86% done and also runs slightly cooler, so it may be the better pick.
Peak 90th pct core temp 37.99 °C (limit 38.0), tightest margin 0.00 °C, 86% of priority-weighted work done.

Hard safety rules:
- Every worker's 90th percentile core temperature must stay below 38.0 °C all shift. Harder work, sun and high WBGT heat people up; 30-min shade rests cool them down.
- Breaks: at most 3 work slots in a row, then a 'rest' slot; at most 2 in a row if any of those slots has WBGT >= 30.0 °C.
- No outdoor tasks during hazards that stop outdoor work. After lightning, outdoor work stays stopped for 30 more minutes.
- Workers who are not acclimatized never do very_heavy tasks when WBGT >= 28.0 °C.
Validity: one entry per slot per worker; off-site workers rest; skills and allowed slots must match.

Peak 90th pct core temp 37.99 °C (limit 38.0), tightest margin 0.00 °C, 86% of priority-weighted work done.

calls.response:
- **Heat is right at the limit.** This plan gets about 86% of the important work done, but on the hottest stretch, crew body temperatures are expected to reach the safety limit with no room to spare. One more hot task or a slower break could push someone over, so watch for heat signs closely, enforce water and shade breaks, and don't add work.

- **Storm stop and new-hire limits are built in.** Everyone comes inside from 1:30 to 3:00 because of lightning and severe thunderstorms. Kofi is new and not used to the heat yet, so he won't be given the hardest physical jobs during the hot part of the day.

- **Two safer options are available.** (1) Give some of the load to Jada, who is currently free, and lighten Kofi's work. This runs slightly cooler but gets a bit less done (about 83%). (2) Move the trenching to the cool morning and save indoor jobs for later. This gets the same 86% done and also runs slightly cooler, so it may be the better pick.
